name: FERRANTI
description: Factuality is important to dialogue summarization. Factual error correction (FEC) of model-generated summaries is one way to improve factuality. Current FEC evaluation that relies on factuality metrics is not reliable and detailed enough. To address this problem, we are the first to manually annotate a FEC dataset for dialogue summarization containing 4000 items and propose FERRANTI, a fine-grained evaluation framework based on reference correction that automatically evaluates the performance of FEC models on different error categories. Using this evaluation framework, we conduct sufficient experiments with FEC approaches under a variety of settings and find the best training modes and significant differences in the performance of the existing approaches on different factual error categories.
reputation: A focused factuality-correction benchmark that is useful for dialogue summarization research, though it is not as broadly established as major summarization benchmarks.
notes: Small, manually annotated dataset centered on factual error correction; performance depends on error category and reference-correction setup.
